pass_a_gloss: It is not unreasonable to use such an example to urge prayer and deter neglect: as no childbearing without wife and the act, so certain things come only to one who so prayed — with such disposition, believing thus, not having so lived before. Rules: no babbling, no small asks, nothing earthly, no anger/troubled reasonings, no prayer without purity-leisure, no forgiveness received without heartily forgiving the asking brother. Benefit accrues many ways to the rightly-praying: first, by praying's very condition he presents himself to a present, overseeing God. As defiling impressions defile reasonings, so remembering the believed God who sees the soul-sanctuary's movements profits — remembrance ordering itself to please the present overseer who outruns every mind, examining hearts/kidneys (Ps 7:10). Even were this the only benefit, reverent self-ordering in prayer's hour is no small gain; its sins avoided and right deeds frequent prayers know by experience. As recalling a wise man spurs emulation and blocks worse impulses, much more does reminding of God the Father of all with prayer profit those persuaded they stand before a present, hearing God.
pass_b_english: Still, it is not unreasonable to employ such an example too, to urge toward praying and deter from neglecting prayer. As there is no begetting children without a wife and the activity taken up for childbearing, so one would not obtain certain things without having so prayed — [obscure clause] with such disposition, believing thus, not having so lived before prayer. One must not babble, then, nor ask small things, nor pray about earthly things, nor come to prayer with anger and troubled reasonings; nor without purity can one conceive leisure arising for prayer; nor can the pray-er obtain forgiveness of sins without heartily forgiving the brother who wronged him and asks pardon.

I hold that benefit comes in many ways to one who prays as one ought, or hastens toward it as he can. First, in any case, he who set his mind toward praying is benefited: by the very condition in praying he presents himself to God, and forms himself to speak to him as present — as overseeing and present. For as such impressions and reminders of certain things defile, concerning the things of which they are reminders, the reasonings born in those impressions — so we must be persuaded it is profitable to remember the believed God who observes the movements in the soul's sanctuary, with remembrance ordering itself to please him as present and overseeing, who reaches before every mind, who examines hearts and searches kidneys. For even if, hypothetically, no further benefit came to one who set his reasoning to pray beyond this one, no small thing must be conceived gained by one who thus reverently ordered himself in prayer's hour. What sins this oft-done thing keeps off, and to what right deeds it bears — those know by experience who gave themselves more constantly to praying. For if reminding and recalling a sensible man profited in wisdom provokes us to zeal for him and often blocks impulses to the worse — how much more does reminding of God, the Father of all, with prayer to him, profit those who persuaded themselves that they stand by and speak to a present and hearing God (Matthew 6:7) (Matthew 6:12) (Psalm 7:10)?
